The '''2025–26 Bundesliga''' was the 63rd season of the [[Bundesliga]], Germany's premier men's [[Association football|football]] competition. [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] were the defending champions. The season began on 22 August 2025  and concluded on 16 May 2026.<ref name="calendar">{{cite web|url=https://www.dfl.de/de/aktuelles/rahmenterminkalender-fur-die-saison-2025-26/|title=Rahmenterminkalender für die Saison 2025/26: Bundesliga-Auftakt am 22. August 2025 – 2. Bundesliga startet am 1. August 2025|website=dfl.de|access-date=8 November 2024 |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Bayern Munich to host RB Leipzig in 2025/26 Bundesliga season opener |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/bayern-munich-host-rb-leipzig-2025-26-new-season-opening-fixture-32821 |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=bundesliga.com - the official Bundesliga website |language=en}}</ref>

On 19 April 2026, Bayern Munich were crowned Bundesliga champions for the 34th time (their 35th overall German title) with four matches to spare following a 4–2 win over [[VfB Stuttgart]].<ref name="Onefootball">{{cite web|url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/official-bayern-munich-crowned-german-champions-42736664|title=Official: Bayern Munich crowned German champions|website=Onefootball|access-date=19 April 2026|language=English|archive-date=20 April 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260420084400/https://onefootball.com/en/news/official-bayern-munich-crowned-german-champions-42736664|url-status=live}}</ref> Bayern also broke their own Bundesliga single-season goals record (101, set in [[1971–72 Bundesliga|1971–72]]) with five matches remaining,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/apr/11/european-football-bayern-munich-barcelona-milan-juventus |title=European football: Bayern break Bundesliga goals record and close on title |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=11 April 2026 |access-date=20 April 2026}}</ref> ultimately finishing the campaign with 122 league goals. Among Europe's [[Big Five (association football)|top five leagues]], this season tally ranks as the second-highest in history, behind only [[Torino FC|Torino]]'s 125 goals in [[1947–48 Serie A|1947–48]] (which had six more matches).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.statmuse.com/fc/ask/most-goals-by-a-team-in-a-season-in-top-5-leagues |title=Most Goals By A Team In A Season In Top 5 Leagues |website=[[StatMuse]] |access-date=16 May 2026 |archive-date=18 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260518204828/https://www.statmuse.com/fc/ask/most-goals-by-a-team-in-a-season-in-top-5-leagues |url-status=live }}</ref> Bayern's 3.59 goals per match is likewise the second-highest in those leagues, trailing only [[Athletic Bilbao]]'s 4.06 goals per game in [[1930–31 La Liga|1930–31]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.statmuse.com/fc/ask/most-goals-per-game-by-a-team-in-a-season-in-top-5-leagues |title=Most Goals Per Game By A Team In A Season In Top 5 Leagues |website=[[StatMuse]] |access-date=16 May 2026 |archive-date=17 May 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260517155400/https://www.statmuse.com/fc/ask/most-goals-per-game-by-a-team-in-a-season-in-top-5-leagues |url-status=live }}</ref>

The fixtures were released on 27 June 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/fixtures-2025-26-release-june-bayern-munich-dortmund-leverkusen-32514|title=When are the 2025/26 Bundesliga and Bundesliga 2 fixtures released?|date=2 June 2025|website=bundesliga.com|language=de|access-date=12 June 2025|archive-date=12 February 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260212105020/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/fixtures-2025-26-release-june-bayern-munich-dortmund-leverkusen-32514|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/fixtures-2025-26-release-june-bayern-munich-dortmund-leverkusen-32514|title=2025/26 Bundesliga and Bundesliga 2 fixtures lists revealed|date=27 June 2025|website=bundesliga.com|language=de|access-date=12 June 2025|archive-date=12 February 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260212105020/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/fixtures-2025-26-release-june-bayern-munich-dortmund-leverkusen-32514|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Hamburger SV]] and [[1. FC Köln]] returned to the Bundesliga after seven and one year absences, respectively. They replaced [[Holstein Kiel]] and [[VfL Bochum]] after spending time in the top flight for one and four years respectively.
